subject.title: [Feature]: Add optional capability descriptors to tool definitions

question: What canonical tool-capability descriptor taxonomy and trust semantics should OpenClaw expose to plugin policy, audit, and Gateway inventory consumers?
rationale: The change would make self-declared tool behavior metadata a public SDK and security-policy input, and it overlaps multiple open capability, provenance, permissions, audit, and Security Matrix proposals that automation cannot reconcile safely.

options.title: Approve advisory descriptor contract
options.body: Define optional unknown-by-default descriptors and project them through tools, plugin metadata, Gateway inventory, trusted policies, and before_tool_call while documenting that declarations are advisory and not grants.

options.title: Fold into broader permissions
options.body: Keep this blocked behind the default-deny capability-permission model so descriptor facts ship only with grants, consent, and enforcement semantics.

options.title: Start with Security Matrix vocabulary
options.body: Use the Security Matrix runtime-fact model as the first canonical consumer before exposing a general public descriptor field.

recommendation.title: Approve advisory descriptor contract
recommendation.body: Define optional unknown-by-default descriptors and project them through tools, plugin metadata, Gateway inventory, trusted policies, and before_tool_call while documenting that declarations are advisory and not grants.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged host-hook contracts PR is the closest current seam for trusted policy and plugin tool metadata decisions.
